# diyalamp

> diyalamp is a free, open-source Markdown editor for macOS. Write with live formatting and save ordinary local Markdown files without an account.

diyalamp edits UTF-8 .md and .markdown files in place. The writing workspace includes tabs, side-by-side notes, folder search, backlinks, Focus mode, and a Pomodoro timer.

## Download and verify

Version 1.4.0 has separate Apple silicon and Intel installers. Both include the runtime. These figures measure the compressed downloads in decimal MB.

- [Apple silicon DMG](https://github.com/diyalamp/diyalamp/releases/download/v1.4.0/diyalamp-1.4.0-macos-arm64.dmg), 45.9 MB (45,912,139 bytes)
- [Apple silicon SHA-256](https://github.com/diyalamp/diyalamp/releases/download/v1.4.0/diyalamp-1.4.0-macos-arm64.dmg.sha256)
- [Intel DMG](https://github.com/diyalamp/diyalamp/releases/download/v1.4.0/diyalamp-1.4.0-macos-x86_64.dmg), 47.5 MB (47,476,062 bytes)
- [Intel SHA-256](https://github.com/diyalamp/diyalamp/releases/download/v1.4.0/diyalamp-1.4.0-macos-x86_64.dmg.sha256)
- [Release notes](https://github.com/diyalamp/diyalamp/releases/tag/v1.4.0)
- [Install and update guide](https://github.com/diyalamp/diyalamp/blob/v1.4.0/docs/install.md)

The [1.3.4 downloads](https://github.com/diyalamp/diyalamp/releases/tag/v1.3.4) measured 48.2 MB (48,239,105 bytes) for Apple silicon and 49.6 MB (49,634,711 bytes) for Intel.

Open the DMG, drag diyalamp into Applications, and choose a folder. The app is ad hoc signed. macOS may block first launch. Writing works offline after installation. To check for updates, choose Help → Check for updates.

## Desktop features

- **Rendered Markdown:** Format text in the editor with headings, emphasis, links, lists, checklists, quotes, inline code, and code blocks. Open the block menu with a slash.
- **Tabs and split view:** Reorder tabs, edit notes side by side, or preview TXT, PDF, JPEG, PNG, GIF, and BMP beside Markdown. The app restores the last workspace’s tab order, selected documents, and split width. Both sidebars are resizable.
- **Local files:** Notes stay in the folder you choose. Autosave checks whether the file changed on disk before writing. Restore deleted notes and folders from File → Deleted items.
- **Workspace search:** Find filenames or note text, including unsaved edits. Use case, whole-word, regular-expression, and path filters.
- **Connected notes:** Use wiki links or relative Markdown links. Navigate the active note’s incoming and outgoing links in the Connections panel.
- **Focus and Pomodoro:** Highlight the active line and dim the surrounding workspace. Run a timed focus and break cycle or repeat it.

## Bring your notes

- **Obsidian:** Open the vault folder as local Markdown. Both apps support local notes without an account. Obsidian offers plugins, Canvas, and a vault-wide graph.
- **Notion:** Export Markdown & CSV and open the resulting folder. Keep the export archive for attachments and databases. Notion offers shared pages, permissions, and databases.
- **Typora:** Open the folder that already contains your Markdown. Typora offers richer rendering for tables, equations, and diagrams.

[Compare editors and see import steps](https://diyalamp.com/alternatives/).
